lines.trans: Every good neighbourhood café needs one hot midday soup and one signature tart.
Did we just get named official menu tasters, Javier?
Best job in the building! Which bowl do we try first, Rocio?
Left spoon: roasted tomato soup with fresh courtyard herbs.
Rich, hot, and great with crusty bread on a rainy afternoon!
Right spoon: golden lentil soup with lemon and olive oil. Even better!
Now try the two lemon tarts: thin pastry on the left, almond on the right.
Oh, the almond crust with Saturday market lemon is unbeatable!

words.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

lines.trans: Save one slice for Mateo, Rocio, or he will lock us out of the kitchen!
So Wednesday's menu is ready: lentil soup, warm bread, tart, and tea.
Simple, homemade, and easy to serve quickly from noon to evening.
Now let us hope it is sunny tomorrow so our paint dries!

Best job in the building! Which bowl do we try first, Rocio?

Rich, hot, and great with crusty bread on a rainy afternoon!
Right spoon: golden lentil soup with lemon and olive oil. Even better!
Now try the two lemon tarts: thin pastry on the left, almond on the right.

Simple, homemade, and easy to serve quickly from noon to evening.
Now let us hope it is sunny tomorrow so our paint dries!

Left spoon: roasted tomato soup with fresh courtyard herbs.
Rich, hot, and great with crusty bread on a rainy afternoon!
Right spoon: golden lentil soup with lemon and olive oil. Even better!
Now try the two lemon tarts: thin pastry on the left, almond on the right.

lines.trans: Save one slice for Mateo, Rocio, or he will lock us out of the kitchen!
So Wednesday's menu is ready: lentil soup, warm bread, tart, and tea.
Simple, homemade, and easy to serve quickly from noon to evening.
Now let us hope it is sunny tomorrow so our paint dries!
See you tomorrow!

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.text: Vamos a la estación ahora.
examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

acabar.gloss: to finish; to have just (acabar de)

meanings.en: to finish; to have just (acabar de)
meanings.note: Acabar de + infinitive means 'to have just done something'.

examples.text: Acabo de llegar del mercado.
examples.trans: I have just arrived from the market.

examples.text: Ya acabamos el trabajo de hoy.
examples.trans: We already finished today's work.

meanings.note: Used both for cooking oil (aceite de oliva) and lubricating oil on hinges.

examples.text: Pon dos gotas de aceite en la bisagra seca.
examples.trans: Put two drops of oil on the dry hinge.

examples.text: Aliñamos la sopa caliente con aceite de oliva.
examples.trans: We dress the hot soup with olive oil.

meanings.note: Ahora mismo means 'right now'.

examples.text: Voy para allá ahora mismo.
examples.trans: I am heading there right now.

examples.text: Ahora tenemos cuatro mesas libres.
examples.trans: Now we have four free tables.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition a + masculine article el; al + infinitive means 'upon doing'.

examples.text: Vamos al mercado por la mañana.
examples.trans: We go to the market in the morning.

examples.text: Al abrir la puerta, sonó el timbre.
examples.trans: Upon opening the door, the bell rang.

meanings.note: Classic Mediterranean baking ingredient in tarts and biscuits.

examples.text: Rocío hornea galletas crujientes de almendra y limón.
examples.trans: Rocio bakes crunchy almond and lemon biscuits.

examples.text: Tostamos las almendras cinco minutos en el horno.
examples.trans: We toast the almonds for five minutes in the oven.

meanings.note: Participle of asar used as an adjective (tomate asado, pimientos asados).

examples.text: La sopa de tomate asado huele de maravilla.
examples.trans: The roasted tomato soup smells wonderful.

examples.text: Servimos verduras asadas con pan recién hecho.
examples.trans: We serve roasted vegetables with freshly baked bread.

meanings.note: Accented aún is interchangeable with todavía.

examples.text: El café aún está caliente.
examples.trans: The coffee is still hot.

examples.text: Aún no han abierto la puerta.
examples.trans: They have not opened the door yet.

meanings.note: Local city district with its own shops and squares.

examples.text: El barrio está aquí.
examples.trans: The neighbourhood is here.

examples.text: Vemos los barrios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the neighbourhoods from the door.

meanings.note: In baking, la base de la tarta means 'the pastry crust / base'.

examples.text: La base de almendra queda dorada y muy crujiente.
examples.trans: The almond crust turns out golden and very crisp.

examples.text: Ponemos una base de fieltro bajo las patas.
examples.trans: We put a felt base under the legs.

meanings.note: Shortens to buen before masculine singular nouns (buen viaje); ¡Buenos días! = Good morning!

examples.text: ¡Buenos días a todos!
examples.trans: Good morning, everyone!

examples.text: Hace muy buen tiempo hoy.
examples.trans: The weather is very nice today.

meanings.note: Plural los cafés (two coffees = dos cafés).

examples.text: ¿Quieres un café con leche?
examples.trans: Do you want a white coffee?

examples.text: Nos vemos en el café de la esquina.
examples.trans: See you at the café on the corner.

meanings.note: Describes hot drinks, food, or water.

examples.text: Me gusta la sopa muy caliente.
examples.trans: I like my soup very hot.

examples.text: ¿Hay agua caliente en la ducha?
examples.trans: Is there hot water in the shower?

meanings.note: From casa ('home'); comida casera and pan casero are warm menu staples.

examples.text: Servimos sopa casera caliente todos los mediodías.
examples.trans: We serve hot homemade soup every day at noon.

examples.text: Esta mermelada casera lleva limones de nuestro árbol.
examples.trans: This homemade jam uses lemons from our tree.

cerrar.gloss: to close; to lock; to turn off (a valve)

meanings.en: to close; to lock; to turn off (a valve)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie: cierro).

examples.text: Cierro la tienda a las ocho.
examples.trans: I close the shop at eight.

examples.text: Anoche cerramos todas las contraventanas.
examples.trans: Last night we closed all the shutters.

meanings.note: Both the kitchen room and the stove/cuisine.

examples.text: La cocina es pequeña pero bonita.
examples.trans: The kitchen is small but pretty.

examples.text: Me encanta la cocina valenciana.
examples.trans: I love Valencian cooking.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.text: Tomo café con leche caliente.
examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.

examples.text: Habla con calma, por favor.
examples.trans: Speak calmly, please.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Es una pieza crujiente.
examples.trans: It is a crispy piece.

examples.text: ¡Hornea muchas esquinas crujientes, cariño!
examples.trans: Bake plenty of corner pieces, my dear!

meanings.note: Table or soup spoon; cucharita is a teaspoon.

examples.text: Pon una cuchara limpia junto a cada cuenco.
examples.trans: Set a clean spoon beside each bowl.

examples.text: Prueba la sopa de lentejas con esta cuchara.
examples.trans: Taste the lentil soup with this spoon.

meanings.note: Deep rounded bowl without handles, often ceramic or wooden.

examples.text: Sirvo la sopa caliente en cuencos blancos.
examples.trans: I serve the hot soup in white bowls.

examples.text: Hay un cuenco lleno de limones sobre la mesa.
examples.trans: There is a bowl full of lemons on the table.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.

examples.text: Soy vecino del barrio.
examples.trans: I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: A la derecha / a mano derecha = on the right.

examples.text: El baño está a la derecha.
examples.trans: The bathroom is on the right.

examples.text: Gira a la derecha en el semáforo.
examples.trans: Turn right at the traffic light.

meanings.note: Marks a starting point in space or time.

examples.text: No hablamos desde aquel domingo.
examples.trans: We have not spoken since that Sunday.

examples.text: Abrimos al público desde mañana.
examples.trans: We open to the public starting tomorrow.

meanings.note: Describes gold colour or golden-brown baked crust.

examples.text: Es una pieza dorada.
examples.trans: It is a golden piece.

examples.text: El del papel dorado del estante de arriba. ¿Por qué?
examples.trans: The one in gold paper from the top shelf. Why?

meanings.note: Los dos / las dos means 'both'.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas azules en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two blue cups on the table.

examples.text: Compra las dos válvulas por favor.
examples.trans: Buy both valves, please.

meanings.note: Multi-storey town building.

examples.text: El edificio está aquí.
examples.trans: The building is here.

examples.text: Vemos los edificios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the buildings from the door.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.text: El patio tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.

examples.text: Pásame el libro de reservas.
examples.trans: Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Desde entonces = since then.

examples.text: ¿Entonces nos vemos mañana a las ocho?
examples.trans: So shall we see each other tomorrow at eight?

examples.text: Desde entonces trabaja con nosotros.
examples.trans: Since then she works with us.

meanings.note: Same singular form for masculine and feminine; plural especiales.

examples.text: La tarta de limón es el postre especial de la casa.
examples.trans: Lemon tart is the house signature dessert.

examples.text: Viernes va a ser una noche muy especial aquí.
examples.trans: Friday is going to be a very special night here.

esperar.gloss: to wait; to wait for; to hope

meanings.en: to wait; to wait for; to hope
meanings.note: Covers both 'wait (for)' and 'hope'.

examples.text: Espere un momento, por favor.
examples.trans: Wait a moment, please.

examples.text: Esperamos que descanse muy bien.
examples.trans: We hope you rest very well.

meanings.note: Pairs with locations (está en el patio) and temporary states (está caliente).

examples.text: El desayuno ya está listo.
examples.trans: Breakfast is ready now.

examples.text: ¿Dónde están las llaves de latón?
examples.trans: Where are the brass keys?

meanings.note: Describes thin glass/fabric as well as fine quality.

examples.text: El cristal de estos vasos es demasiado fino para el té.
examples.trans: The glass of these cups is too thin for tea.

examples.text: Corta el limón en rodajas muy finas.
examples.trans: Cut the lemon into very thin slices.

meanings.note: Pintura fresca = wet paint; agua fresca = cool water.

examples.text: Compramos pescado fresco en el mercado.
examples.trans: We buy fresh fish at the market.

examples.text: Por la noche hace fresco.
examples.trans: At night it's cool.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine; plural fáciles.

examples.text: La receta de la tarta de limón es muy fácil.
examples.trans: The lemon tart recipe is very easy.

examples.text: Esta cerradura nueva se abre muy fácil.
examples.trans: This new lock opens very easily.

guardar.gloss: to keep; to put away; to guard

meanings.en: to keep; to put away; to guard
meanings.note: Everyday verb for putting something safely away in a pocket or cupboard.

examples.text: Guardo las llaves en este cajón.
examples.trans: I keep the keys in this drawer.

examples.text: Te guardé el último rollo de canela.
examples.trans: I saved the last cinnamon roll for you.

hacer.gloss: to do; to make; ago (hace + time)

meanings.en: to do; to make; ago (hace + time)
meanings.note: Irregular: hago, hice, hecho; hace tres años = three years ago.

examples.text: La panadera hace pan fresco cada mañana.
examples.trans: The baker bakes fresh bread every morning.

examples.text: Llegó hace diez minutos.
examples.trans: She arrived ten minutes ago.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.text: Sigue recto hasta el puente.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.

examples.text: Nos quedamos hasta el viernes.
examples.trans: We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: Garden herbs or meadow grass.

examples.text: La hierba está aquí.
examples.trans: The herb is here.

examples.text: Vemos las hierbas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the herbs from the door.

meanings.note: Same singular form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: El aroma del pan recién horneado es insuperable.
examples.trans: The aroma of freshly baked bread is unbeatable.

examples.text: Rocío prepara una sopa de lentejas insuperable.
examples.trans: Rocio makes an unbeatable lentil soup.

meanings.note: A la izquierda = on/to the left.

examples.text: La izquierda está aquí.
examples.trans: The left is here.

examples.text: Vemos las izquierdas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lefts from the door.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.

examples.text: La habitación tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.text: Las ventanas dan al jardín.
examples.trans: The windows face the garden.

examples.text: Desayunamos a las ocho.
examples.trans: We have breakfast at eight.

meanings.note: Usually plural (lentejas) when referring to lentil soup or stew.

examples.text: Una sopa caliente de lentejas reconforta en invierno.
examples.trans: A hot lentil soup is comforting in winter.

examples.text: Cocemos las lentejas a fuego lento con verduras frescas.
examples.trans: We simmer the lentils slowly with fresh vegetables.

meanings.note: Plural limones.

examples.text: Un té con limón, por favor.
examples.trans: A tea with lemon, please.

examples.text: En el patio hay un limonero lleno de limones.
examples.trans: In the courtyard there's a lemon tree full of lemons.

meanings.note: With estar, means 'ready / all set'; with ser, means 'smart'.

examples.text: El té caliente ya está listo.
examples.trans: The hot tea is ready now.

examples.text: Es una arquitecta muy lista.
examples.trans: She is a very smart architect.

meanings.note: Versatile everyday noun for door keys, shut-off valves, and spanners.

examples.text: ¿Me das la llave de la habitación?
examples.trans: Can you give me the room key?

examples.text: He perdido las llaves de casa.
examples.trans: I've lost my house keys.

meanings.note: Bajo la lluvia = in the rain.

examples.text: La lluvia es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The rain is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la lluvia.
examples.trans: We talk about the rain.

meanings.note: Bread or pastry dough.

examples.text: La masa es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The dough is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la masa.
examples.trans: We talk about the dough.

meanings.note: La mañana = the morning; mañana (without article) = tomorrow.

examples.text: Por la mañana servimos café caliente.
examples.trans: In the morning we serve hot coffee.

examples.text: ¡Hasta mañana a las ocho!
examples.trans: See you tomorrow at eight!

meanings.note: Al mediodía = at noon.

examples.text: El mediodía es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The noon is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el mediodía.
examples.trans: We talk about the noon.

meanings.note: Irregular comparative/superlative of bueno; plural mejores.

examples.text: Esta ventana tiene la mejor vista.
examples.trans: This window has the best view.

examples.text: Hoy el radiador calienta mejor.
examples.trans: Today the radiator heats better.

meanings.note: Plural menús; menú del día is Spain's classic midday set menu.

examples.text: Escribimos el menú del miércoles en la pizarra.
examples.trans: We write Wednesday's menu on the board.

examples.text: El menú incluye sopa caliente, pan crujiente y té.
examples.trans: The menu includes hot soup, crusty bread, and tea.

meanings.note: Covered food market in a Spanish neighbourhood.

examples.text: Compro la fruta en el mercado.
examples.trans: I buy fruit at the market.

examples.text: El mercado central abre a las ocho.
examples.trans: The central market opens at eight.

meanings.note: Invariable in plural: el miércoles, los miércoles.

examples.text: El miércoles está aquí.
examples.trans: The Wednesday is here.

examples.text: Vemos los miércoles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the Wednesdays from the door.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Necesito un bolígrafo para firmar.
examples.trans: I need a pen to sign.

examples.text: ¿Necesitan ustedes alguna toalla más?
examples.trans: Do you all need another towel?

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Te nombramos encargado oficial de las luces del patio.
examples.trans: We appoint you officially in charge of the courtyard lights.

examples.text: El libro antiguo nombra a cada huésped por su apellido.
examples.trans: The old book names each guest by surname.

nos.gloss: us; to us; each other (¡Nos vemos!)

meanings.en: us; to us; each other (¡Nos vemos!)
meanings.note: First-person plural object/reflexive/reciprocal pronoun.

examples.text: ¡Nos vemos mañana por la mañana!
examples.trans: See you tomorrow morning!

examples.text: Nos alegra mucho la noticia.
examples.trans: The news makes us very glad.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with the thing possessed (nuestro patio, nuestra posada).

examples.text: Nuestra posada tiene ocho habitaciones.
examples.trans: Our guesthouse has eight rooms.

examples.text: Nuestros vecinos toman café aquí.
examples.trans: Our neighbours have coffee here.

meanings.note: Becomes u before words starting with o- or ho-.

examples.text: ¿Prefieres café o té caliente?
examples.trans: Do you prefer coffee or hot tea?

examples.text: ¿Abrimos hoy o esperamos a mañana?
examples.trans: Do we open today or wait until tomorrow?

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine singular; plural oficiales.

examples.text: Mañana recibimos la carta oficial del ayuntamiento.
examples.trans: Tomorrow we receive the official letter from City Hall.

examples.text: Hoy es la apertura oficial de nuestra sala de té.
examples.trans: Today is the official opening of our tea room.

meanings.note: Expresses surprise or realization.

examples.text: ¡Oh, ahí está la puerta azul!
examples.trans: Oh, there is the blue door!

examples.text: Oh, perdona, no te había visto.
examples.trans: Oh, sorry, I had not seen you.

meanings.note: In Valencia and eastern Spain, oliva is used alongside aceituna for the olive fruit.

examples.text: Un chorrito de aceite de oliva realza las lentejas.
examples.trans: A drizzle of olive oil brings out the lentils.

examples.text: Traemos aceite de oliva virgen del mercado local.
examples.trans: We bring virgin olive oil from the local market.

meanings.note: Plural los panes; pan recién hecho = freshly baked bread.

examples.text: Compro pan todas las mañanas.
examples.trans: I buy bread every morning.

examples.text: ¿Me pasas el pan, por favor?
examples.trans: Can you pass me the bread, please?

meanings.note: Marks destination, recipient (para ti), deadline, and minutes to the hour (cinco para las doce).

examples.text: Este paquete blanco es para mi hermano.
examples.trans: This white parcel is for my brother.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para las doce.
examples.trans: It is ten minutes to twelve.

meanings.note: Traditional inner courtyard at the heart of a Spanish building.

examples.text: Los niños juegan en el patio.
examples.trans: The children play in the courtyard.

examples.text: Desayunamos en el patio cuando hace sol.
examples.trans: We have breakfast in the courtyard when it's sunny.

meanings.note: Used alone as 'Perfect!'.

examples.text: ¡Perfecto, hasta mañana!
examples.trans: Perfect, see you tomorrow!

examples.text: Hace un tiempo perfecto para pasear.
examples.trans: It's perfect weather for a walk.

meanings.note: Pintura fresca = wet paint.

examples.text: Necesitamos pintura blanca para el baño.
examples.trans: We need white paint for the bathroom.

examples.text: Me encanta la pintura española.
examples.trans: I love Spanish painting.

meanings.note: Shortens to primer before masculine singular nouns (el primer día); also used as adverb ('first').

examples.text: Hoy es mi primer día de trabajo.
examples.trans: Today is my first day of work.

examples.text: La primera habitación está libre.
examples.trans: The first room is vacant.

meanings.note: From probar ('to taste / try'); feminine plural probadoras.

examples.text: Hoy los dos hermanos son nuestros probadores de sopas.
examples.trans: Today the two brothers are our soup tasters.

examples.text: Un buen probador distingue enseguida el limón fresco.
examples.trans: A good taster immediately spots fresh lemon.

probar.gloss: to try; to taste; to test

meanings.en: to try; to taste; to test
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: pruebo).

examples.text: Prueba este pan con aceite de oliva.
examples.trans: Try this bread with olive oil.

examples.text: Ayer probamos la mermelada de manzana.
examples.trans: Yesterday we tasted the apple jam.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.text: Espero que descanses muy bien.
examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

qué.gloss: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)

meanings.en: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)
meanings.note: Used in questions (¿qué hora es?) and exclamations (¡qué alivio!).

examples.text: ¿Qué hora es ahora mismo?
examples.trans: What time is it right now?

examples.text: ¡Qué mañana tan luminosa!
examples.trans: What a bright morning!

meanings.note: With food and drink, ¡qué rico! is the most natural Spanish way to say 'how delicious!'.

examples.text: Esta tarta casera de limón está muy rica.
examples.trans: This homemade lemon tart is delicious.

examples.text: La miel de otoño tiene un sabor rico y suave.
examples.trans: Autumn honey has a rich, smooth flavour.

meanings.note: Used both as adjective and adverb (corre rápido).

examples.text: El tren es muy rápido.
examples.trans: The train is very fast.

examples.text: Hablas muy rápido, más despacio, por favor.
examples.trans: You speak very fast; more slowly, please.

se.gloss: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one

meanings.en: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one
meanings.note: Reflexive, reciprocal, passive/impersonal pronoun, and indirect object le/les before lo/la.

examples.text: La puerta se abre despacio.
examples.trans: The door opens slowly.

examples.text: Aquí se oye el canto de los pájaros.
examples.trans: Here you can hear the birds singing.

secar.gloss: to dry; to wipe dry (secarse = to dry out)

meanings.en: to dry; to wipe dry (secarse = to dry out)
meanings.note: Spelling changes c -> qu before -e (sequé, seque).

examples.text: Seca bien las bisagras antes de dar la pintura.
examples.trans: Dry the hinges thoroughly before applying paint.

examples.text: Con este sol la ropa tendida se seca enseguida.
examples.trans: In this sunshine the hanging laundry dries right away.

meanings.note: En palabras sencillas = in plain words.

examples.text: La receta es muy sencilla.
examples.trans: The recipe is very simple.

examples.text: Quiero algo sencillo para cenar.
examples.trans: I want something simple for dinner.

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.

examples.text: Esa maleta azul es mía.
examples.trans: That blue suitcase is mine.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> i: sirvo, sirve, sirvió).

examples.text: Servimos desayuno caliente de ocho a diez.
examples.trans: We serve hot breakfast from eight to ten.

examples.text: La encargada sirvió tres tazas de té de menta.
examples.trans: La encargada served three cups of mint tea.

meanings.note: Hace sol = it is sunny.

examples.text: Hoy hace sol.
examples.trans: It's sunny today.

examples.text: Me siento al sol en el patio.
examples.trans: I sit in the sun in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Hecho una sopa = soaked through.

examples.text: La sopa está aquí.
examples.trans: The soup is here.

examples.text: Vemos las sopas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the soups from the door.

meanings.note: El sábado means 'on Saturday'; los sábados means 'on Saturdays'.

examples.text: Los sábados vamos temprano al mercado de la plaza.
examples.trans: On Saturdays we go early to the market in the square.

examples.text: Este sábado abrimos las ventanas de la galería.
examples.trans: This Saturday we open the sunroom windows.

meanings.note: Por la tarde = in the afternoon; ¡Buenas tardes! = Good afternoon!; llegar tarde = arrive late.

examples.text: ¡Buenas tardes! ¿Tienen una habitación libre?
examples.trans: Good afternoon! Do you have a room free?

examples.text: Perdón por llegar un poco tarde.
examples.trans: Sorry for arriving a little late.

meanings.note: Usual word in Spain for a sweet tart or birthday cake.

examples.text: Hay tarta de chocolate para el postre.
examples.trans: There is chocolate cake for dessert.

examples.text: Mi abuela hace una tarta de manzana riquísima.
examples.trans: My grandmother makes a delicious apple tart.

meanings.note: Todo el día = the whole day; todo el mundo = everyone; sobre todo = mostly.

examples.text: Todo está limpio y en su sitio.
examples.trans: Everything is clean and in its place.

examples.text: Camina todo recto por esta calle.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead down this street.

meanings.note: Staple ingredient of Mediterranean soups, salads, and toast.

examples.text: Compramos tomates maduros en el puesto de la esquina.
examples.trans: We bought ripe tomatoes at the corner stall.

examples.text: Asamos los tomates con ajo y ramas de tomillo.
examples.trans: We roast the tomatoes with garlic and thyme sprigs.

meanings.note: Ir al trabajo = go to work.

examples.text: El trabajo está aquí.
examples.trans: The work is here.

examples.text: Vemos los trabajos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the works from the door.

meanings.note: Un trozo de bizcocho = a piece of cake.

examples.text: El trozo está aquí.
examples.trans: The piece is here.

examples.text: Vemos los trozos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pieces from the door.

meanings.note: Accented té ('tea') distinguishes the noun from pronoun te ('you').

examples.text: Tomo un té verde por la tarde.
examples.trans: I have a green tea in the afternoon.

examples.text: ¿Prefieres té o café?
examples.trans: Do you prefer tea or coffee?

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.

examples.text: Son las siete y cuarto.
examples.trans: It is quarter past seven.
